notes: Rates stayed mostly between about 2.8% and 4.6% through most of 2017, then spiked to 12.4% in November 2017.
Early 2018 saw the highest rates of the window: 14.13% in February and 18.96% in March.
The most recent months show lower rates again, at 1.16% in June 2018 and 3.38% in July 2018, before rising to 6.19% in August 2018.

assumptions: Trend is shown as a monthly series of the late-delivery rate (late orders / delivered orders) over the analysis window Jan 2017 - Aug 2018.
Late rate uses only delivered orders, per the glossary.
Months flagged is_partial are included but marked so results can carry the warning.
definitions: Delivered order: status delivered and a delivery timestamp exists
Late: delivered date after the estimated date (dates, not timestamps)
Order month: month of the purchase timestamp

caveats: The series is volatile month to month, so short-term movements should be read with caution.
January 2017 has a much smaller delivered-order count (750) than later months.

evidence.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT o.purchase_month AS month, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE o.is_delivered) AS delivered_orders, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE o.is_late) AS late_orders FROM analytics.orders AS o WHERE o.purchase_month BETWEEN CAST('2017-01-01' AS DATE) AND CAST('2018-08-01' AS DATE) GROUP BY o.purchase_month) SELECT m.month, m.delivered_orders, m.late_orders, ROUND(100.0 * m.late_orders / NULLIF(m.delivered_orders, 0), 2) AS late_rate_pct, dc.is_partial FROM monthly AS m JOIN analytics.data_coverage AS dc ON dc.month = m.month WHERE dc.in_analysis_window ORDER BY m.month LIMIT 501

headline: The late-delivery rate has been volatile, ranging from 1.16% in June 2018 to 18.96% in March 2018, with no clear sustained direction.
